cards.text: Pile (from bottom to top) 1 vegetable, reed, clay, wood, vegetable, stone, grain, reed on this card. At any time, you may buy the top item for 1 food.

cards.name: Guildmaster
cards.text: You receive 4 wood when you acquire the Joinery or play the Cabinetmaker. When you acquire the Pottery or play the Potter, you receive 4 clay. When you acquire the Basketmaker's Workshop or play the Basketmaker, you receive 3 reed. If you have already played any of these cards when you play the Guildmaster, you receive 2 building resources of the appropriate type for each existing card.

cards.name: Head of the Family
cards.text: You can use any room building or family growth action space, even if another player has already placed a person on it.

cards.name: Hedge Keeper
cards.text: Whenever you build at least 1 fence, you can build 3 additional fences without paying any additional wood.

cards.name: Hobby Farmer
cards.text: When you play this card, you receive 1 vegetable that you may sow immediately if you have an empty plowed field.

cards.name: Hut Builder
cards.text: Play this card during round 1--4. At the start of round 11, you can extend your hut by 1 room at no cost, as long as you have not yet renovated to a stone house.

cards.name: Land Agent
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Take 1 Vegetable" action space, you also receive 1 grain. When you play this card, you receive 1 vegetable from the general supply.

cards.name: Lord of the Manor
cards.text: At the end of the game, you receive 1 bonus point for each scoring category where you have scored the maximum 4 points.

cards.name: Maid
cards.text: Once you have built a clay hut, place 1 food on each remaining round space. At the start of these rounds, you receive the food.

cards.name: Mason
cards.text: Once during the game, at any time after your stone house reaches at least 4 rooms, you may extend it by 1 room at no cost.

cards.name: Master Baker
cards.text: Whenever another player bakes bread, you can bake bread if you have a baking improvement with the “baking” symbol. If you take a bake action yourself, you receive 1 additional food.

cards.name: Master Brewer
cards.text: In the feeding phase of each harvest, the Master Brewer can convert up to 1 grain to 3 food.

cards.name: Master Builder
cards.text: Once during the game, at any time after your home reaches at least 5 rooms, you may extend it by 1 room at no cost.

cards.name: Master Forester
cards.text: Include the "2 Wood" action card from the 3-player game as an additional forest. At the start of each round, place 2 wood on the card. Any player who uses this action space must pay you 2 food.

cards.name: Master Shepherd
cards.text: Place 1 sheep on each of the next 3 round spaces. At the start of these rounds, you receive the sheep.

cards.name: Meat Seller
cards.text: If you have an oven, you can convert your animals into food at any time. Take 2 food for each sheep, 3 for each wild boar and 4 for each cattle.

cards.name: Mendicant
cards.text: At the end of the game, you can discard up to 2 begging cards without losing points for them.

cards.name: Merchant
cards.text: Whenever you use a “minor improvement” or “minor or major improvement” action, you can pay 1 food to use the action a second time.

cards.name: Mushroom Collector
cards.text: Whenever you use a person's action to take wood that is lying on an action space, you can leave 1 of that wood on the space and receive 2 food in exchange.

cards.name: Pastor
cards.text: If, when you play this card or later in the game, you are the last player to have only 2 rooms in your home, you receive 3 wood, 2 clay, 1 reed and 1 stone.

cards.name: Patron
cards.text: In future, whenever you play an occupation, you receive 2 food before you pay the costs of the occupation.

cards.name: Plough Driver
cards.text: Once you have a stone house, you can pay 1 food at the start of each round to plough (at most) 1 field.

cards.name: Plough Maker
cards.text: Whenever you use either of the "Plough 1 Field" or "Plough Field and Sow" action spaces, you can pay 1 food to plough 1 additional field.

cards.name: Potter
cards.text: In each harvest, the Potter can convert up to 1 clay to 2 food.

cards.name: Quarryman
cards.text: You can use the Quarryman at any time to convert stone to food. For each stone you convert, you receive 2 food.

cards.name: Ratcatcher
cards.text: In rounds 10 and 12, all other players may not place 1 of their family's offspring (if they have any). This card may only be played until the end of Round 9.

cards.name: Reed Collector
cards.text: Place 1 reed on the next 4 round spaces. At the start of these rounds, you receive the reed.

cards.name: Renovator
cards.text: Pay 2 less clay to renovate to a clay hut, and pay 2 less stone to renovate to a stone house.

cards.name: Seasonal Worker
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Day Labourer" action space, you receive 1 additional grain. From round 6 onwards, you can choose to receive 1 vegetable instead.

cards.name: Shepherd
cards.text: During each harvest, if you have at least 4 sheep during the breeding phase, you receive 2 lambs instead of 1 as long as you have room for them.

cards.name: Stablehand
cards.text: Whenever you build at least 1 fence, you also receive 1 stable which you must build immediately.

cards.name: Stablemaster
cards.text: One (and only one) of your unfenced stables may hold up to 3 animals of the same type.

cards.name: Stockman
cards.text: You receive 1 cattle when you build your second stable, 1 wild boar when you build your third and 1 sheep when you build your fourth.

cards.name: Stone Carrier
cards.text: Whenever you take stone with an action of a person, you can also take 1 additional stone. If you also receive other building resources, this costs you 1 food.

cards.name: Stonecutter
cards.text: All improvements, rooms and renovations cost you 1 stone less.

cards.name: Storyteller
cards.text: Whenever you use the “Traveling Players” action on an action space, you can leave 1 food on the space and receive 1 vegetable instead.

cards.name: Tenant Farmer
cards.text: You immediately receive a loan of one of each type of animal. Before scoring, return the 3 animals. For each animal that you cannot or do not want to return, you lose 1 point.

cards.name: Thatcher
cards.text: Pay 1 reed less to build each room, for each renovation, and for each of the Water Mill, Half-timbered House, Chicken Coop, Holiday House, Mansion and Corn Storehouse.

cards.name: Turner
cards.text: At any time, you can use the Turner to convert any number of wood to 1 food each.

cards.name: Tutor
cards.text: At the end of the game, you receive 1 bonus point for each occupation that you play after this one.

cards.name: Undergardener
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Day Labourer" action space, you also receive 1 vegetable.

cards.name: Woodcutter
cards.text: You receive 1 additional wood whenever you use a person's action to take wood.

cards.name: Wooden Hut Builder
cards.text: At the end of the game, you receive 1 bonus point for each room in your wooden hut.

cards.name: Yeoman Farmer
cards.text: At the end of the game, you only lose points for unused farmyard spaces and begging cards.

cards.name: Alternative Designer
cards.text: Whenever you build stables or fences, you may replace wood with the same amount of clay or stone. Whenever you build rooms, you may replace wood with the same amount of clay or stone, to a maximum of 2 clay and 2 stone.

cards.name: Animal Farmer
cards.text: At the end of the game, you receive 1 bonus point for each of your pastures that cannot contain any more animals than it does. If all of your pastures qualify, you receive 1 additional bonus point.

cards.name: Animal Holder
cards.text: If there are still 1/3/6/9 rounds to play, you immediately receive 1/2/3/4 wood. At the end of the game, each player who has the most animals receives 3 bonus points.

cards.name: Apprentice
cards.text: At the beginning of every harvest, you receive 1 food for every major improvement you own worth at least 2 points without counting bonus points.

cards.name: Architect
cards.text: Whenever you extend your home, you receive 2 food for each new room. Whenever you build stables, you receive 1 food for each new stable.

cards.name: Artisan
cards.text: At most once per harvest, when you use an improvement to convert a building resource to food, you receive 2 additional food.

cards.name: Astronomer
cards.text: When you play this card, you receive 2 food. Whenever 3/4/5 of your family members (or guests) use 3/4/5 adjacent action spaces (forming a vertical or horizontal line), you receive 1/3/5 bonus points. The action spaces must have the same size.

cards.name: Auctioneer
cards.text: Place 2 reed, 3 wood, 3 clay, and 2 stone on rounds 7, 9, 11 and 13, respectively. At the start of these rounds, all players simultaneously bid food for the resources. The highest bidder gets the resources and you get the food. If you win, pay your food to the general supply. Ties are broken by this round's player order.

cards.name: Baker's Daughter
cards.text: If another player plays the Baker or Master Baker, you may play this card immediately at no cost. You can use the "Take 1 Grain" and "Sow and Bake Bread" action spaces even if another player has placed a person on the space. When you play this card, you can immediately take a bread baking action.

cards.name: Bard
cards.text: Whenever another player uses the “Traveling players” action on an action space, you receive 1 food and 1 wood from the general supply.

cards.name: Businesswoman
cards.text: When you play this card, immediately play up to 2 improvements (any combination of major and minor) by paying their costs.

cards.name: Carrot Cake Baker
cards.text: Whenever you convert vegetables into food, you may additionally take a bread baking action. The Carrot Cake Baker can also convert 1 vegetable into 2 food at any time.

cards.name: Carrot Farmer
cards.text: Place 3 vegetables from the general supply on this card. Whenever you use the "Plough 1 Field" action space, you may pay 1 food for one of the vegetables.

cards.name: Clay Starter
cards.text: When you play this card, if you only have 2 rooms in your wooden hut, immediately pay 1 food to renovate it to clay for free.

cards.name: Early Riser
cards.text: When you play this card, you receive 1 sheep. For you, the breeding phase of the harvest precedes the field and feeding phases. You may immediately cook baby animals if you do not have room to keep them.

cards.name: Family Counselor
cards.text: Whenever at the end of a work phase all of your adult family members were placed on the same game board, you receive 1 food/1 grain/1 vegetable if it were 2/3/4+ adults.

cards.name: Fence Helper
cards.text: Whenever another player takes a fence building action, you may pay that player 1 food to immediately take a fence building action too.

cards.name: Fish Seller
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Fishing" action, you may use food that you take from that action space to buy up to 2 items. One building resource costs 1 food. One grain, sheep or wild boar costs 2 food. One vegetable or cattle costs 3 food.

cards.name: Fisherman's Apprentice
cards.text: Whenever another player uses the "Fishing" action, you may pay that player 1 food to play an occupation.

cards.name: Food Critic
cards.text: The next time you use the "Fishing" action, place 1 food from the general supply on this card. Whenever you convert animals, vegetables, grain, or building resources to food, you may place that good on this card. At the end of the game, you receive 1/2/4/6 bonus points for 4/5/6/7+ different items on this card.

cards.name: Freeloader
cards.text: Each round, your first family member may use an occupied action space. Your first family member can never take the "Starting Player" action space.

cards.name: Glass Blower
cards.text: If you have an oven, the Glassblower may convert 1/2 clay to 3/5 food in each harvest.

cards.name: Glutton
cards.text: In the feeding phase of the last harvest after feeding your family normally, you may pay 3 additional food for 1 bonus point, up to a maximum of 6 bonus points.

cards.name: Grafter
cards.text: During the breeding phase of harvest, if you have 2 or more grain in your personal supply, you receive 1 grain from the general supply. If you have 2 or more vegetables, you receive 1 vegetable from the general supply.

cards.name: Grain Farmer
cards.text: Whenever you have at least 1/4/7/10 planted grain at the beginning of the field phase of a harvest, you receive 1/2/3/4 food.

cards.name: Grain Lover
cards.text: If there are still 7 full rounds to play, you may plow 1 field, which you may immediately sow with 1 grain from your personal supply. At the end of the game, all players with the most total grain receive 2 bonus points each.

cards.name: Grump
cards.text: If there are still 1/3/6/9 rounds to play, you immediately receive 1/2/3/4 wood. At the end of the game, all players with the fewest family members receive 2 binus points each.

cards.name: Harbor Master
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Fishing" action space, you receive 1 additional reed. Whenever another player uses the "Fishing" action space, you receive 1 reed and 1 food from the general supply.

cards.name: Headmaster
cards.text: Whenever another player plays an occupation, place 1 food from the supply on this card. Whenever you play an occupation, you may pay any costs using food from this card. At the end of a 4/5 player game, you receive 1 bonus point for every 3/4 food on this card.

cards.name: Helper
cards.text: You can use any “Renovate”, “Build room(s)” or “Major Improvement” action space, even if another player has already placed a person on it.

cards.name: Hermit
cards.text: At the end of the game, you receive 6 bonus points if this is the only occupation you have played.

cards.name: Hobbyist
cards.text: Whenever another player plays an occupation, you may pay 1 food to the general supply to play 1 minor improvement, or 2 food to build 1 major improvement.

cards.name: Hoe Maker
cards.text: Whenever you build at least 1 fence, you may also pay 1 food to plough 1 field.

cards.name: Inventor
cards.text: All improvements with a printed cost of 4 or more resources cost you 1 less resource of your choice.

cards.name: Job Seeker
cards.text: Once in play, this card does not count as an occupation for any purpose. Whenever, at the start of a round, you have fewer occupations than any 2 other players, you may pay 1 food to immediately play an occupation.

cards.name: Late Bloomer
cards.text: Whenever you have fewer family members than all of the other players and you have room in your home, you may immediately take a “family growth” action. You need room in your home for the offspring. Place the offspring in an empty room. This family member is not considered a newborn and may take an action the same round.

cards.name: Late Sleeper
cards.text: At the start of each round, announce whether or not you will sleep late. If you sleep late, you place all of your people after everyone else has placed all of theirs, but you may also place a guest token.

cards.name: Master Baker's Apprentice
cards.text: When you play this card, mark a revealed action space with an arrow marker. This action space now has the added text “and/or bake bread”. Whenever another player bakes bread using this space, you receive 1 food from the general supply. When you play this card, you may also take a bread baking action.

cards.name: Mathematician
cards.text: From round 6 on, if there are wood spaces with the same amount of wood after refilling each round (at the end of phase 2), you can take 1 wood from one of those spaces. This also applies to clay action spaces. In 5 player games, this also applies to stone action spaces. You can take only 1 resource per round.

cards.name: Miner
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Day Labourer" action space, you can take all the stone markers from one of the "1 Stone" action spaces (stage 2 or stage 4) in the returning home phase (phase 4).

cards.name: Mooch
cards.text: When you play this card, choose another player. Until the end of the next harvest, you may convert animals, vegetables, grain, and building resources to food as if you owned the chosen player's improvements in addition to yours.

cards.name: Oldest Occupation
cards.text: From round 5 on, whenever any player uses the "Day Labourer" action space, they may pay you 2 food to immediately take a “family growth” action.

cards.name: Opportunist
cards.text: Whenever you use your last action in a round to take one or more types of building resources that have not yet been taken this work phase, you receive 1 additional resource of one of those types.

cards.name: Pearl Seeker
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Fishing" action space you receive 1 additional stone. Also, you can use food that you take from that action space to buy more stone. Each stone costs 2 food.

cards.name: Pilgrim
cards.text: You receive 2 food before you pay the costs of playing this occupation. At the start of a round, if you have no building resources, you may take 1 building resource from the general supply; if you have no food, you may take 1 food from the general supply.

cards.name: Pond Watchman
cards.text: At the end of a work phase, after all other players have taken their actions, you may pay 1 food to move one of your people that used the "Fishing" action this round to an unoccupied wood accumulating action space and take that action.

cards.name: Resource Collector
cards.text: Place 1 wood, 1 clay, 1 reed, and 1 stone on the next 4 round spaces in any order you choose. At the start of those rounds, you receive the resource.

cards.name: Ringmaster
cards.text: When you use the “Traveling Players” action, you may either play a minor improvement or you may pay 1 grain to build a major improvement immediately afterward.

cards.name: Seed Master
cards.text: At any time, you may pay 1 food to convert 1 grain in your personal supply to 1 vegetable. At any time, you may convert 1 vegetable in your personal supply to 1 grain.

cards.name: Singer
cards.text: When you play this card, you receive 2 building resources of your choice.

cards.name: Stone Deliveryman
cards.text: Place 1 stone on each of the spaces for rounds 8, 10, 12, and 14. At the start of these rounds, you receive the stone.

cards.name: Stone Trader
cards.text: Whenever you use an action to take stone, you may immediately afterward pay 1 food to play an improvement that has a printed stone cost.

cards.name: Stonepiler
cards.text: Whenever you build fences or stables, you may pay some or all of the cost in stone with each stone worth 2 wood.

cards.name: Tax Collector
cards.text: Whenever another player pays building recources to build a major improvement, you receive 1 resource of those paid (of your choice). You may pay 1 food to the general supply to receive another of the resources paid.

cards.name: Truffle Digger
cards.text: Whenever you use a family member's action to take wood that is on an accumulating action space and you have 1/2/3 wild boar, you receive 1/2/3 additional food.

cards.name: Understudy
cards.text: Whenever an action space is occupied by exactly one of your family members, you may use that action space again with a second family member.

cards.name: Vegetarian
cards.text: For each grain or vegetable you convert to food (in any manner), you receive 1 additional food. You may not convert animals to food for the rest of the game.

cards.name: Village Farmer
cards.text: If there are still 1/3/6/9 rounds to play, you immediately receive 1/2/3/4 wood. At the end of the game, all players who have the most plowed fields receive 3 bonus points each.

cards.name: Wheedler
cards.text: Whenever you receive food from an action space, you receive 1 additional food. This benefit does not apply to food gained due to an improvement or occupation.

cards.name: Wintercrafter
cards.text: Between the field and feeding phases of each harvest, you may play a minor improvement or pay 2 food to build a major improvement.

cards.name: Animal Dealer
cards.text: Whenever you use one of the "1 Sheep", "1 Wild Boar" or "1 Cattle" action spaces, you can pay 1 food to take 1 additional animal of that type.

cards.name: Bricklayer
cards.text: Pay 1 less clay for each improvement and renovation. Pay 2 less clay for each room.

cards.name: Businessman
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Starting Player" action space, you can play an additional minor or major improvement after you play the minor improvement.

cards.name: Butcher
cards.text: You can convert your animals into food at any time. You receive 1 food for each sheep, 2 for each wild boar and 3 for each cattle.

cards.name: Cabinetmaker
cards.text: In each harvest, the Cabinetmaker can convert up to 1 wood to 2 food.

cards.name: Chamberlain
cards.text: At the start of round 11 (or immediately, if you play this card after the start of Round 11), turn over the round cards for the remaining rounds. You (and only you) can use these actions immediately; the other players must wait until the appropriate round.

cards.name: Clay Digger
cards.text: Include the "1 Clay" action card from the 3-player game as an additional clay pit. Immediately place 3 clay on the card and add 1 clay at the start of each round. Any player who uses this action must pay you 3 food.

cards.name: Clay Hut Builder
cards.text: Once you live in a clay hut, place 2 clay on each of the next 5 round spaces. At the start of these rounds, you receive the clay.

cards.name: Clay Plasterer
cards.text: Renovating your wooden hut to a clay hut costs you only 1 clay and 1 reeds. Each room of your clay hut costs you 3 clay and 2 reeds.

cards.name: Corn Profiteer
cards.text: You can convert 1 grain to 3 food at any time. Any other player can prevent this by buying the grain from you for 2 food. If more than one player wants to buy, you choose one of them.

cards.name: Cowherd
cards.text: Whenever you use the "1 Cattle" action space, you receive 1 additional cattle from the general supply.

cards.name: Farm Steward
cards.text: Once you live in a clay hut or stone house, play your next family growth action as a “family growth even without room”.

cards.name: Fence Builder
cards.text: When you play this card, place one of your fences on an action space of your choice. If you use an action on this action space, you can also build fences as an additional action.

cards.name: Fence Deliveryman
cards.text: Add 6 and 10 to the number of the current round. Place 4 of your fences on each corresponding round space. At the start of these rounds, you can pay 2 food to build all 4 fences immediately.

cards.name: Fencer
cards.text: Whenever another player builds 1 to 4 fences, you receive 1 wood from the general supply. Whenever another player builds 5 or more fences, you receive 2 wood.

cards.name: Field Watchman
cards.text: Whenever you use the action space "Take 1 Grain", you can also plough up to 1 field.

cards.name: Field Worker
cards.text: Whenever another player sows one or more fields, you receive 1 grain in a 3-player game or 1 food in a 4 or 5 player game.

cards.name: Fieldsman
cards.text: Whenever you sow 1 field, place 2 additional goods of the same type from the general supply on the stack. Whenever you sow 2 fields, place 1 extra good on each.

cards.name: Gardener
cards.text: Take vegetables from the general supply and not from your vegetable field whenever you harvest them --- you keep the vegetables on the fields.

cards.name: Groom
cards.text: Once you have a stone house, you can build 1 stable at the beginning of each round at a cost of 1 wood. You do not need to place a family member on an action space to do this.

cards.name: Harvest Helper
cards.text: At the start of the feeding phase in each harvest, you can take 1 grain from 1 field belonging to another player. That player receives 2 food from the general supply.

cards.name: Hide Farmer
cards.text: At the end of the game, you can pay 1 food each for any number of unused farmyard spaces. These do not lose you points in the scoring.

cards.name: Juggler
cards.text: Whenever you use the “Traveling Players” action on an action space, you can choose to receive twice as much food as is on the card. If you do this, you must give one food each to the owners of the Magician, Conjurer, Street Musician, Puppeteer, Acrobat, Dancer, Animal Trainer and Storyteller.

cards.name: Layabout
cards.text: Once you have played this card, you may not take part in the next harvest.

cards.name: Manservant
cards.text: When you build a stone house, place 3 food on each remaining round space. At the start of these rounds, you receive the food.

cards.name: Market Crier
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Take 1 Grain" action space, you can take an additional 1 grain and 1 vegetable. If you do this, the other players each receive 1 grain from the general supply.

cards.name: Midwife
cards.text: Whenever another player has offspring and then has a larger family than you, you receive 1 food. If they have at least 2 more family members than you, you receive 2 food.

cards.name: Milking Hand
cards.text: In the field phase of the harvest, you receive food if you have cattle, without having to give up the cattle: for 5 or more cattle, 3 food; for 3 or 4 cattle, 2 food; for 1 cattle, 1 food. At the end of the game, you receive 1 bonus point for every 2 cattle.

cards.name: Net Fisherman
cards.text: If one of your people uses an action space that directly provides reeds, you can take all food from the "Fishing" action space in the returning home phase (phase 4).

cards.name: Outrider
cards.text: Whenever you use the most recent round card with one of your people, you receive 1 additional grain.

cards.name: Pig Breeder
cards.text: Your wild boar breed at the end of round 12, if there is room for the piglet. When you play this card, you receive 1 wild boar.

cards.name: Pig Catcher
cards.text: Whenever you use a person to take wood that is on an action space, you can leave 2 of that wood on the space and receive a wild boar instead.

cards.name: Puppeteer
cards.text: Whenever another player chooses the “Traveling players” action on an action space, you can pay 1 food to play an occupation.

cards.name: Rancher
cards.text: Whenever, at the start of a round, you are using more farmyard spaces than every other player, you receive 1 wood.

cards.name: Reed Buyer
cards.text: Whenever reed is taken for the first time in a round, you may give the player who takes it 1 food in exchange for 1 of the reed. The other player receives an additional 1 food from the general supply as compensation.

cards.name: Sheep Whisperer
cards.text: Add 4, 7, 9 and 11 to the number of the current round and place 1 sheep on each corresponding round space. At the start of these rounds, you receive the sheep.

cards.name: Social Climber
cards.text: Whenever you are the first player to renovate to a clay hut or a stone house, you receive 3 stone. If you are the second, you receive 2 stone; the third, you receive 1 stone.

cards.name: Stone Buyer
cards.text: Whenever stone is taken for the first time in a round, you may give the player who takes it 1 food in exchange for 1 of the stone. The other player receives an additional 1 food from the general supply.

cards.name: Stone Carver
cards.text: In each harvest, the Stone Carver can convert up to 1 stone to 3 food.

cards.name: Street Musician
cards.text: You receive 1 grain whenever another player takes the “Traveling Players” action on an action space.

cards.name: Sycophant
cards.text: Any other player that uses the "Take 1 Grain" action space must first pay you 1 food. In addition, you receive 1 food from the general supply. You receive that food even when you take the grain yourself.

cards.name: Taster
cards.text: Whenever another player is the starting player, you can pay them 1 food at the start of the round and be the first to place a family member. After that, play starts with the starting player as usual.

cards.name: Water Carrier
cards.text: Once any player has built the Well, place 1 food on the remaining round spaces. At the start of these Rounds, you receive the food.

cards.name: Well Builder
cards.text: For you, the Well is now a minor improvement and costs only 1 stone and 1 wood to build.

cards.name: Wood Buyer
cards.text: Whenever another player receives wood from an action, you can buy 1 wood from them for 1 food (even without their agreement).

cards.name: Wood Collector
cards.text: Place 1 wood on each of the next 5 round spaces. At the start of these rounds, you receive the wood.

cards.name: Acrobat
cards.text: Whenever you use the “Traveling players” action on an action space, after all of the players have finished their turns you may move that person to one of the "Take 1 Grain", "Plough 1 Field" and "Plough Field and Sow" action spaces, if it's free, and take the action.

cards.name: Adoptive Parents
cards.text: When you take a family growth action, you can pay 1 food to immediately place the offspring in your home. This allows you to take an action with it this round. If you do this, the offspring does not count as “newborn”.

cards.name: Animal Breeder
cards.text: Whenever you fence unused spaces to create at least one new pasture, you can buy a pair of animals: 2 sheep for 1 food, 2 wild boar for 2 food, or 2 cattle for 3 food.

cards.name: Animal Handler
cards.text: Place 1 sheep on the space for round 7, 1 wild boar on round 10 and 1 cattle on round 14. At the start of these rounds, you can buy the animal for 1 food.

cards.name: Animal Tamer
cards.text: You can keep 1 animal in each room of your home. You may keep more than 1 type of animal in your home.

cards.name: Animal Trainer
cards.text: Whenever you take food from a “Traveling players” space, you may immediately use it to buy animals: Pay 2 food for each sheep or wild boar and 3 food for each cattle.

cards.name: Basin Maker
cards.text: For each wild boar that you convert into food, you can place up to 2 wood from your personal supply on this card. At the end of the game, you receive 1 bonus point for each wood on this card except the 1st, 4th, 7th and 10th.

cards.name: Brushwood Collector
cards.text: You may replace the required reed with a total of 1 wood for any renovation or for each new room. (You use brushwood to make the roof.)

cards.name: Cattle Breeder
cards.text: Your cattle breed at the end of round 12, if there is space for the calf. When you play this card, you receive 1 cattle.

cards.name: Clay Worker
cards.text: Whenever you use an action of a person to take wood or clay, you also receive 1 additional clay.

cards.name: Constable
cards.text: You receive wood immediately when you play this card: if played in round 12 or 13, take 1 wood; if played in round 9, 10, or 11, take 2 wood; if played in round 6, 7, or 8, take 3 wood; if played before round 6, take 4 wood. At the end of the game, any player who has no negative points receives 5 bonus points.

cards.name: Countryman
cards.text: After all players have placed their people, you may move one of your people from a "Take 1 Grain" or "Take 1 Vegetable" action space to a free action space with a “sow” action.

cards.name: Educator
cards.text: Whenever another player plays an occupation card, you can pay 3 food to play one yourself. From your 4th occupation, this only costs 2 food.

cards.name: Foreman
cards.text: At the start of the work phase of each round, you can place 1 food from the general supply on an action space of your choice.

cards.name: Forester
cards.text: Whenever you use a sowing action, you can plant wood on this card. There can be up to 3 stacks of wood on this card, as shown. The wood is treated the same as sown grain and is harvested during the Field phase.

cards.name: Frame Builder
cards.text: In each renovation, you may replace exactly 1 clay or 1 stone with 1 wood. In each extension, you may replace exactly 2 clay or 2 stone with 1 wood.

cards.name: House Steward
cards.text: You receive wood immediately when you play this card: if played in round 12 or 13, take 1 wood; if played in round 9, 10, or 11, take 2 wood; if played in round 6, 7, or 8, take 3 wood; if played before round 6, take 4 wood. At the end of the game, the player(s) with the most rooms in their home receive 3 bonus points each.

cards.name: Lover
cards.text: When you play this card, immediately carry out a “Family growth even without room” action (similar to the round card from stage 5). Playing this card costs you an additional 4 food.

cards.name: Magician
cards.text: Whenever you use your last person to choose the “Traveling Players” action on an action space, you receive an additional 1 grain and 1 food.

cards.name: Manufacturer
cards.text: Once you have a clay hut or a stone house, the Joinery, Pottery and Basketmaker's Workshop are minor improvements for you and their cost is reduced by 2 building resources of your choice.

cards.name: Market Woman
cards.text: Whenever you receive vegetables through a person's action or through a minor improvement, you receive an additional 2 grain.

cards.name: Organic Farmer
cards.text: At the end of the game, you receive 1 bonus point for each of your pastures [ref] that contains at least 1 animal, but could contain at least 3 more animals than it does.

cards.name: Perpetual Student
cards.text: Whenever you can play an occupation card, you can ask another player to randomly draw one of your occupation cards instead of choosing one yourself. If you do this, you receive 3 food before you pay the costs of the card, but you must play the card that the other player draws.

cards.name: Pieceworker
cards.text: Whenever you receive wood, clay, reed, stone or grain on an action space, you can buy one more of the same good for 1 food. Whenever you receive vegetable(s) on an action space, you can buy one more for 2 food.

cards.name: Pig Whisperer
cards.text: Add 4, 7 and 10 to the number of the current round and place 1 wild boar on each corresponding round space. At the start of these rounds, you receive the wild boar.

cards.name: Ploughman
cards.text: Add 4, 7 and 10 to the number of the current round and place 1 field on each corresponding round space. At the start of these rounds, you can plough that field by paying 1 food.

cards.name: Resource Seller
cards.text: Pile (from bottom to top) 1 stone, clay, stone, clay, reed, clay, wood on this card. You receive the top marker when you receive that type of building resource.

cards.name: Schnaps Distiller
cards.text: In the feeding phase of each harvest, you can convert up to 1 vegetable to 5 food.

cards.name: Scholar
cards.text: Once you have a stone house, at the start of a round you can always either pay 1 food to play an occupation card or play an improvement card by paying its costs.

cards.name: Seed Seller
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Take 1 Grain" action space, you receive 1 additional grain. When you play this card, you receive 1 grain.

cards.name: Serf
cards.text: Whenever you use the "Sow and Bake Bread" action space, you receive 1 grain before taking the action(s). Alternatively, you can exchange 1 grain for 1 vegetable.

cards.name: Sheep Farmer
cards.text: Whenever you take sheep with one of your people, you receive an additional sheep from the general supply. You can exchange 3 sheep for 1 cattle and 1 wild boar at any time (except during the breeding phase).

cards.name: Shepherd Boy
cards.text: Once you live in a stone house, place 1 sheep on each remaining round space. At the start of these rounds, you receive the sheep.

cards.name: Slaughterman
cards.text: Whenever another player converts 1 or more animals into food, you receive 1 food from the general supply. In the feeding phase of the harvest, you are the last player to feed your family (so you can benefit if other players slaughter).

cards.name: Stone Breaker
cards.text: At any time, you can renovate your clay hut to a stone house without using a “Renovation” action space.

cards.name: Storehouse Clerk
cards.text: Whenever you have at least 5 stone at the start of a round, you receive 1 extra stone. If you have at least 6 reed, you receive 1 reed. If you have at least 7 clay, you receive 1 clay. If you have at least 8 wood, you receive 1 wood.

cards.name: Storehouse Keeper
cards.text: Whenever you use a person's action to take reed and stone at the same time, you also receive your choice of 1 clay or 1 grain.

cards.name: Tanner
cards.text: When you convert wild boar or cattle to food, place them on this card. At the end of the game, you receive bonus points if you have animal markers on this card. For the wild boar on this card, you receive: 6 or more wild boar, 3 points; 4 or 5 wild boar, 2 points; 2 or 3 wild boar, 1 point. For the cattle on this card, you receive: 4 or more cattle, 3 points; 3 cattle, 2 points; 2 cattle, 1 point.

cards.name: Tinsmith
cards.text: You can convert clay into food at any time. You receive 1 food per clay. If any player has built a Well, you receive 3 food for each 2 clay instead.

cards.name: Traveling Salesman
cards.text: Whenever you select a “minor improvement” action on an action space, you can play a major instead of a minor improvement. If you select a “major or minor improvement” action on an action space, you can play 2 minor improvements.

cards.name: Veterinarian
cards.text: When you play this card, place 4 sheep cubes, 3 wild boar cubes and 2 cattle cubes in a container. At the start of each round, draw two animals. If they are the same, keep one. Return the 1 or 2 animals to the container.

cards.name: Weaver
cards.text: Whenever you have at least 2 sheep at the start of the work phase of a round, you receive 1 food.

cards.name: Wet Nurse
cards.text: Whenever you build room(s), you may grow your family by up to the number of rooms that you build, if you have the room to house the new family members. This costs 1 food per person.

cards.name: Wood Carver
cards.text: In each round, you pay 1 wood less for one of the following: an improvement, a room of a wooden hut, a stable or a fence.

cards.name: Wood Deliveryman
cards.text: Place 1 wood on each remaining space for rounds 8 to 14. At the start of these rounds, you receive the wood.

cards.name: Cooper
cards.text: Whenever you or another player receives 3 food or more on an action space, you receive 1 food from the general supply.

cards.name: Cube Cutter
cards.text: During the field phase of each harvest, you can exchange 1 wood and 1 food for 1 bonus point.

cards.name: Dance Instructor
cards.text: You receive 4 food before you pay the costs of playing this occupation. You may immediately return this card to your hand after you have played it.

cards.name: Game Designer
cards.text: You can exchange 1 wood, 1 clay, 1 reed and 1 stone for 2 food and 1 bonus point at any time and as often as you like.

cards.name: Gentleman
cards.text: Whenever you manage to be the very last player to place a person in any round, you receive 1 food after you take the final action. If you play this occupation with the last person to be placed during the current round, you receive 2 food.

cards.name: Herald
cards.text: At any time, you may look at all the remaining unplaced round cards and re-sort them. When you play this card, you receive 2 wood.

cards.name: Mail Coach Driver (English)
cards.text: From now until the end of the game, the other players only receive goods from action spaces when they return their people to their home.

cards.name: Mail Coach Driver (German)
cards.text: From now until the end of the game, the other players do not receive goods and food during the work phase, but only when they return their people to their home.

cards.name: Mother of Twins
cards.text: When you have family growth, you can pay 3 food to bring 2 new family members instead of 1 into the game. You do not need to have space in your home for the second new family member.

cards.name: Seed Trader
cards.text: Place 2 grain and 2 vegetables on this card. You may buy them at any time. Each grain costs 2 food, each vegetable costs 3 food.

cards.name: Sower (English)
cards.text: You may immediately sow each vegetable that you receive outside the harvest phase and would otherwise place in your supply.

cards.name: Sower (German)
cards.text: You may immediately sow each grain that you receive outside the field phase of a harvest and would otherwise place in your supply.

cards.name: Taxidermist
cards.text: When you convert animals to food, you can place some or all of them on this card instead of returning them to the general supply. The card can hold a maximum of 1 sheep, 1 wild boar and 1 cattle. These animals are counted in scoring.

cards.name: Village Beauty
cards.text: At any time, you can pay 3 food to take a family growth action without placing one of your people. You must have room in your home. You can use the newborn to take actions from the following round.

cards.name: Action Artist
cards.text: Whenever you use the “Traveling Players” action on an action space, you can return 1 animal of your choice to the general supply and receive 4 food in exchange.

cards.name: Big Backer
cards.text: Whenever another player receives 2 or more animals of one type, you can buy one from him. A sheep costs 2 food, a wild boar 3 food, a cattle 4 food.

cards.name: Building Tycoon
cards.text: Whenever another player builds at least one room, you can give him 1 food and immediately build exactly one room yourself.

cards.name: Child Prodigy
cards.text: Whenever you have family growth, you can immediately pay 1 wood for 1 bonus point, or 2 wood for 2 bonus points.

cards.name: Environmentalist
cards.text: Whenever you play or buy an improvement, you can replace 1 building resource of your choice with 1 wood.

cards.name: Family Singers
cards.text: During the action phase, you can place any number of people on the family singers space instead of on an action space. For each person you place on the space, you receive 1 bonus point.

cards.name: Lovable Vagabond
cards.text: Whenever you have no more food during the feeding phase of a harvest and should take one or more begging cards, you receive one fewer begging card.

cards.name: Magnate
cards.text: When you play this card, you immediately receive 2 stone. At the end of the game, the player(s) with the most building resources receive(s) 3 bonus points.

cards.name: Opinion Leader
cards.text: At the start of each round, you can mark one action space of your choice with an arrow (claim) marker. Each player can use this action space during this round. (This cannot be used on action spaces on which goods are placed). Remove the arrow marker at the end of each round.

cards.name: Ski Instructor
cards.text: Whenever another player has family growth, he must pay you 1 food (or beg the food, if necessary). You must immediately turn the Ski Instructor face-down when you grow your family. You no longer receive its benefits, but it still counts as a played occupation.

cards.name: Therapist
cards.text: When you play this card, you can pay 2 food to immediately play 1 further occupation. Whenever another player plays an occupation, you can pay him 1 food. He must then, if possible, play a different occupation card instead.

cards.name: Waltzer
cards.text: You can place 2 people one after another, as long as both action spaces are on the same board and adjoin one another (not diagonally).
